title: Tiered shard compaction and per-tenant retention controls for audit pipeline
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: We need a per-tenant retention and tiered shard compaction subsystem for the audit ingestion pipeline. Current ingestion writes uniform time-based shards and applies a global TTL which causes disproportionate cost for low-activity tenants and slows queries for high-activity tenants. This ticket implements: (1) per-tenant retention policy enforcement exposed to admins via RBAC v2, (2) tiered compaction that moves cold segments to compacted coldstore and reduces index resolution, and (3) automated cost-aware retention overrides that throttle older, low-value events to reduce storage spend.
technical_design: High level: add a Retention Controller service that subscribes to ingestion metadata and tenant billing signals. The controller will compute per-tenant policy (default -> 90 days; sensitive tenants -> configurable 365 days; low-spend tenants -> floor 14 days). Shards: keep time-based primary shards but add logical tenant buckets and a compaction layer that triggers compaction into two compacted formats: CompactIndex (queryable summary for 14-90 day window) and ArchiveBlob (coldstore for > retention). Compaction triggers: idle_time > X, shard_size > Y, tenant_cost_per_day < Z, or admin override. Integration with RBAC v2: admin roles can set tenant retention via Admin Console API; changes are audited and SSO/SAML users map to RBAC groups. Storage: index metadata contains compaction_level tag; query router will fall back to CompactIndex when full shard unavailable. Backfill/migration: offline job to scan last 18 months and compact according to new policies, with throttling to keep write amplification < 10% and not exceed current ingest throughput. Metrics: compaction lag, bytes-moved, coldstore growth, query-95 latency for audit search, and cost per GB/day. Security: must preserve tamper-evidence header and append-only ledger pointers for audit entries moved to archive. Feature gated behind runtime flag "tiered_audit_retention".
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind tiered_audit_retention. 2) Deploy Retention Controller in staging with read-only mode to collect signals for 72h. 3) Canary on internal org: enable compaction for 2 tenants with retention overrides set by Eng. Monitor CPU, compaction throughput, search latency, and correctness. 4) Expand to 20 orgs (mix of high-, medium-, low-activity). 5) Enable admin Console UI to set per-tenant policies (RBAC enforced). 6) Run migration job for orgs that opt-in; schedule maintenance windows for large tenants. 7) Full rollout with automatic cost-aware overrides enabled for tenants with monthly spend < $50/user equivalent. 8) Post-rollout: 30-day observation and revert plan prepared.
acceptance_criteria: Retention Controller deployed and respects per-tenant policies from Admin API
Compaction moves segments to CompactIndex and ArchiveBlob with preserved audit integrity headers
Query router seamlessly routes to compacted data with <20% P95 latency increase on affected queries
Admin Console UI allows RBAC v2-authorized admins to update retention; changes generate audit events
Migration job can compact 6 months of data for a 10TB tenant within defined throttles without exceeding 80% of ingestion capacity
Automated tests for compaction logic, retention enforcement, and admin RBAC checks are present and passing
Security review completed and tamper-evidence verification added to archive retrieval flow
testing_strategy: Unit tests for retention policy evaluation, integration test for Retention Controller + ingestion metadata stream, e2e staging canary with synthetic traffic, load tests that measure compaction write amplification, and cross-team QA verifying RBAC permissions and SSO mappings. Create a synthetic tenancy harness that simulates 1000 tenants spanning high/low activity to validate cost heuristics. Add chaos test to simulate compactor node restart during compaction to validate idempotency.
